key_insight: A learning-guided search loop can discover new extremal geometric constructions faster than manual design, and modest expert seeding can push bounds beyond fully automated search.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests ML-assisted instance generation can improve lower-bound discovery for combinatorial optimization, aiding algorithm design and worst-case analysis.
method: Adapt PatternBoost: alternate local search with transformer-based candidate generation (Axplorer).
Represent geometric instances, define search moves, and train surrogate models to rank candidates before exact verification.
Tested on three geometry problems: rectangle independent set gaps, stabbing unit squares, and recursive guillotine cutting.
evidence_signal: The method found non-trivial constructions and improved the stabbing-unit-squares gap from the literature best of 3/2 to 20/13, then to 14/9 with structured staircase seeding.
watch_item: Performance depends strongly on representation quality and initial instance diversity, and purely automated search quickly plateaus on harder bounds.
paper_title: Towards Learning-Guided Discovery of Extremal Geometric Constructions: A PatternBoost Study
